significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that subliminal transfer has a measurable capacity threshold whose location scales with "steering-vector orthogonality, dataset size, and layer count" rather than semantic trait similarity. This would establish both a multi-trait behavioral phenomenon—"transfer degrades gracefully then collapses"—and a geometric, partly causal account of interference, fixing predictions for unseen trait combinations and resource settings rather than merely identifying another transmissible trait. A verified-false result would distinguishably rule out this proposed finite-capacity/geometric explanation, although the bundling of several scaling variables means that rejection of only one sub-hypothesis would be less decisive. Cloud et al.'s source work establishes transmission through semantically unrelated data but leaves channel limits consequentially unresolved; after substituting the claim with the bare topic, this capacity law disappears, so the score is supported by claim-specific content rather than subliminal learning's general importance.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claimed "capacity ceiling," the "pairwise cosine similarity" interference predictor, and the design rule that "packing traits into disjoint layers raises the ceiling." These are potentially ex ante: an auditor or pipeline operator could estimate packing risk from trait-vector geometry and resource settings before distillation, while a model builder or attacker could alter layer allocation before producing the outcome. Because the conclusion is framed as scaling and predictive relations, re-extraction on a new model would test predicted structure rather than merely repeat a search for an unspecified direction, though its asserted scope remains limited to steering-vector-mediated subliminal transmission and may require model-specific calibration. Topic substitution would remove all three handles and leave no forecast or design rule, so the reach comes from this claim rather than from the broader topic; it plausibly serves people auditing or shipping distillation pipelines, but does not yet warrant reach outside AI or across unrelated hidden-channel mechanisms.
